findings.title: Reachable vulnerable dependency github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go v3.2.0+incompatible (CVE-2020-26160)
findings.detail: govulncheck reported GO-2020-0017 (CVE-2020-26160 / GHSA-w73w-5m7g-f7qc) as REACHABLE: the seed calls jwt.MapClaims.VerifyAudience (trace: main.go:43 sca.parseToken calls jwt.MapClaims.VerifyAudience). If a JWT contains an audience claim with an array of strings rather than a single string, and MapClaims.VerifyAudience is called with req set to false, audience verification is bypassed, allowing an invalid set of audiences. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N (7.5).
findings.recommendation: Migrate off the abandoned github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go to github.com/golang-jwt/jwt (fixed in 4.0.0-preview1 lineage) or a maintained successor.

findings.title: Reachable vulnerable dependency golang.org/x/text v0.3.0 (CVE-2022-32149)
findings.detail: govulncheck reported GO-2022-1059 (CVE-2022-32149 / GHSA-69ch-w2m2-3vjp) as REACHABLE: the seed calls golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage (trace: main.go:51 sca.matchLanguage calls language.ParseAcceptLanguage). An attacker may cause a denial of service by crafting an Accept-Language header which ParseAcceptLanguage takes significant time to parse. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H (7.5).
findings.recommendation: Upgrade golang.org/x/text to v0.3.8 or later.

findings.title: Reachable vulnerable dependency golang.org/x/text v0.3.0 (CVE-2021-38561)
findings.detail: govulncheck reported GO-2021-0113 (CVE-2021-38561 / GHSA-ppp9-7jff-5vj2) as REACHABLE: the same call to golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage reaches this vulnerability (both GO-2022-1059 and GO-2021-0113 list ParseAcceptLanguage as the vulnerable symbol). Due to improper index calculation, an incorrectly formatted language tag can cause Parse to panic via an out-of-bounds read, usable as a denial-of-service vector on untrusted input. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H (7.5).
findings.recommendation: Upgrade golang.org/x/text to v0.3.7 or later.
